user:
Project: React. Upgrade being assessed: 17 -> 18.
This change was introduced in release 18. Source: How to Upgrade to React 18 (official_migration_guide). Section: Configuring Your Testing Environment.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
When you first update your tests to use createRoot, you may see this warning in your test console: The current testing environment is not configured to support act(...) To fix this, set globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT to true before running your test: // In your test setup file globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true;
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Configuring Your Testing Environment: When you first update your tests to use createRoot, you may see this warning in your test console: The current testing environment is not configured to support act(...) To fix this, set globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT to true before running your test: // In your test setup file globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true; The purpose of the flag is to tell React that it's running in a unit test-like environment. React will log helpful warnings if you forget to wrap an update with act. You can also set the flag to false to tell React that act isn't needed. This can be useful for end-to-end tests that simulate a full browser environment. Eventually, we expect testing libraries will configure this for you automatically. For example, the next version of React Testing Library has built-in support for React 18 without any additional configuration. More background on the act testing API and related changes is available in the working group.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 18 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 18 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: Test environment missing IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT flag with createRoot
paths.description: When tests are updated to use createRoot in React 18, a warning appears in the test console that the testing environment is not configured to support act(...). Setting globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true in the test setup file resolves it. Setting it to false tells React that act isn't needed, which can be useful for end-to-end tests.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses React 18, where tests using createRoot may warn about act environment configuration
quotes: When you first update your tests to use createRoot, you may see this warning in your test console
conditions.relevance: The warning appears once tests move to the React 18 createRoot API.

quotes: When you first update your tests to use createRoot
conditions.relevance: The warning is triggered when tests use createRoot.

conditions.statement: The test setup does not set globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT
quotes: set globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT to true before running your test
conditions.relevance: Without the flag, React warns that the testing environment is not configured to support act.

conditions.statement: A testing library version with built-in React 18 support configures the flag automatically
conditions.expected_value: React Testing Library with built-in React 18 support
quotes: the next version of React Testing Library has built-in support for React 18 without any additional configuration
conditions.relevance: If the testing library configures this automatically, no manual action is needed.
ambiguities: The text does not state which React Testing Library version number includes the built-in support.

suggested_actions: Add globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true; to the test setup file for unit test environments.
For end-to-end tests simulating a full browser, consider setting globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = false so React knows act isn't needed.
Upgrade to a React Testing Library version with built-in React 18 support.
